source.title: Do Models Hear Like Us? Probing the Representational Alignment of Audio LLMs and Naturalistic EEG
source.authors: Hao-Yu Yang; Xin Xiao; Jiang Zhong; Yu Tian; Xiao Dong; Yu Mao; Hao Wu; Kaiwen Wei

record.tranche_reason: The study measures EEG–Audio LLM alignment using multiple similarity metrics and two datasets, and reports that metric choice and dataset change the observed alignment. It does not test whether independently trained models converge toward one another as they scale.
record.gate_note: The study reports model-to-EEG alignment, not similarity between independently trained models. Only findings bearing on V6 are included. The paper also reports time-window, emotion, and TNC findings, but those do not test the listed convergence versions. Table 1's flattened numeric layout does not reliably associate all values with metric columns, so the rows below use the values and qualitative results explicitly assigned to metrics in the text.
record.test_reason: The study measures Audio LLM–human EEG correspondence, not convergence between independently trained models. Metric-dependent rankings of models by brain similarity do not measure model-to-model similarity. Consequently, these results do not test V6 or any other listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that EEG–Audio LLM correspondence depends on depth, metric and prosodic condition, with metric-dependent model rankings and stronger geometric alignment at 250–500 ms. They also report lower cross-dataset rank scores. These conclusions concern model–brain correspondence, not convergence between models.
record.recipe_differences: Measures alignment of Audio LLM representations with human EEG using within-sentence RDM comparisons; does not compare independently trained models to each other or test scale-dependent inter-model convergence.
record.method_sensitivity: Strongly metric-dependent rankings and peak layers; absolute rank-based scores shift across the two EEG datasets. Prosodic condition also changes reported metrics.

fits_no_version.finding: Similarity metrics yield different model rankings and peak layers for Audio LLM–EEG correspondence. For example, Alice Spearman RSA favors GLM-4-Voice (0.2031), whereas dCor favors Ultravox-8B (0.4722).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Conclusions about Audio LLM alignment with human EEG depend on the similarity metric and model layer.

fits_no_version.finding: Rank-based EEG–model peaks are systematically lower on ds004408, while dependence scores are comparable or higher. Ultravox-8B Spearman falls from approximately 0.138 to 0.081, while dCor rises from approximately 0.472 to 0.570.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: EEG–Audio LLM correspondence varies across naturalistic listening datasets, with distinct shifts for rank and dependence measures; these datasets also differ in recording setup and participants.

record.problems: Model-to-brain alignment is not model-to-model convergence. No capability or performance measure is related to alignment. The text gives peak estimates without per-peak uncertainty in the trajectory descriptions; Table 1's extracted layout is flattened and does not permit reliable assignment of all values. The two datasets differ in content and recording setup, so their contrast does not isolate a single input-data factor.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports additional metric trajectories for all 12 models and both datasets, plus affect-group and electrode/time-window analyses. These were not separately extracted where the text did not give a metric-specific result that could be assigned unambiguously; Table 1 is flattened in the supplied text. The affect and time-window results do not bear on the listed convergence versions.

untested.parts: All: no inter-model alignment measured as a function of size or capability across architectures, objectives or training data.
All: no vision–language model comparison on paired images and captions or capability-dependent alignment.
All: no comparisons across random initializations of the same architecture.
All: no representation mapping, stitching, transfer-loss or interchangeability experiment between models.
All: no recurring interpretable features or circuits identified across models.

All within the claim's inter-model scope: metric and dataset sensitivity are measured only for model–brain correspondence; no inter-model metric, neighbourhood or out-of-distribution sensitivity is tested.
All: no completeness or plateau of inter-model convergence measured, and no test attributing it to shared training data or objectives.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to the listed claim versions because the comparison target is human EEG. This does not deny the reported EEG alignment. Cross-metric peak values are comparison measures, not null baselines, and different metric magnitudes alone do not demonstrate sensitivity. No claim-relevant results are missing; additional time-window, affect and TNC analyses were declared in rows_left_out and remain outside the versions.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test convergence between independent models as a function of model size, capability, architecture, objectives, or data.
Does not compare vision and language models on paired images and captions.
Does not compare same-architecture models trained from different initializations or examine shared features or subspaces.
Does not test mappings, stitching, relative representations, or alignment without paired data between models.
Does not identify recurring interpretable features or circuits across models.

Tests metric and dataset dependence for EEG–model alignment. Does not vary neighbour count, test out-of-distribution inputs, or establish whether model-to-model convergence changes under these choices.
Does not test whether inter-model alignment plateaus or whether common training data or objectives explain such alignment.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Across the tested models and datasets, comparing rank-based geometry with dependence-based metrics
reader_labels.reason: The study reports that metric rankings and peak layers differ, including early/intermediate Spearman peaks alongside later or larger dependence peaks (rows A2S–A12D and N2S–N12D).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Cross-dataset comparison on ds004408 versus Alice in Wonderland
reader_labels.reason: The authors report lower rank-based peaks on ds004408 and comparable or higher dependence-style scores; examples include Audio-Flamingo-3 and both Ultravox checkpoints (rows A1S, A11S, A12S, N1S, N11S, N12S).
